annotationRationale: The question tests justified power cycles modulo 10. Remainders locate the exponents within those cycles; the other supplied computations do not warrant a separate method.

review.questionCheck: The statement, choices and key agree. The two powers end in 8 and 9, so their sum ends in 7, choice A. No figure is needed.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: One explained digit-cycle method is sufficient. The supplied modular computations are equivalent reductions or longer calculations, rather than a beneficial distinct route.
review.annotationCheck: Power cycles are correctly assessed, with congruence and remainder arithmetic as support. No contextual concepts or national alignments need to be forced.

methodReviews.mathCheck: Multiplication depends only on the factors' units digits. The deterministic cycles 2,4,8,6 and 3,9,7,1 each repeat after four powers. The exponent remainders are 3 and 2, selecting 8 and 9. Their sum has units digit 7.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: The cited LIVE explanation and AoPS digit-cycle solutions support this route. The candidate supplies independent explanatory prose and explicitly justifies repetition, avoiding the unexplained exponent reduction in AoPS Solution 1. source-informed-original is accurate.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The explanation establishes why only units digits matter, why each cycle repeats and how the exponent remainder selects a position. No modular notation or advanced exponent theorem is needed.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: math:modular-powers precisely captures the justified cycles. math:modular-congruence is appropriate support for units-digit sums/products and remainder reduction, even without congruence notation.
